data.body:
AC EVIDENCE, verified against merged main (Gerrit 2093), each on the criterion's OWN stated command rather than a paraphrase.

AC1 correctness and edge-cases each have an explicit routing entry and appear in registry.effective_criteria(): pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py, 13 passed. Both keys are present in the packaged criteria_routing.json with blocking_enabled true.
AC2 numeric budget: same run - every blocking_enabled criterion listed in the document table parses <= 8.0 percent of all changes, and every row marked hold has blocking_enabled false. The assertion is in that pytest run and fails if a listed blocking row exceeds the budget.
AC3 grep -c '^## Code-v4 friction replay at 0.54' prints 1 (was 0).
AC4 --block-impact column correctness: covered corpus-free by the unit test feeding block_impact() a synthetic in-memory corpus with known priorities, asserting would_block, changes_hit, of_all_changes and mean_validity.
AC5 degrades safely with no corpus: calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py --block-impact correctness=0.54 --tracker /nonexistent exits 0 - an empty corpus prints a zero-row table instead of dividing by zero.
AC6 grep -c '^_BLOCKING_SET = (' docs/experiments/replay_code_v4_would_block.py prints 0 (was 1), so the blocking set is no longer hard-coded.
AC7 replay_code_v4_would_block.py still exits 0 with no corpus.

Note on identity, since this ticket sits on a colliding prefix: this is 4144-2784-6437-4efb, alias tireless-ruinable-prairiedog, one of the epic's nine named HARDENING children - so the epic's no-behaviour-change and net-negative-lines guarantees do not apply to it. It is NOT 4144-75d3-6af1-47d3 (tireless-convenable-canvasback, 'enrich gate marker is all-or-nothing'), which has no parent and is outside this epic. My own board tooling keyed tickets by their 4-hex prefix earlier in this run and briefed an agent with the wrong ticket's title as a result; the canonical id was always correct.
